topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.1, what is the declared policy of the Commonwealth regarding fair housing?
choice_a: To regulate only commercial real estate, not residential housing
choice_b: To provide fair housing only to citizens who meet income requirements
choice_c: To provide fair housing to all citizens regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, elderliness, familial status, source of funds, sexual orientation, gender identity, military status, or disability
choice_d: To defer entirely to federal fair housing law with no state-level protections
explanation: Virginia's fair housing policy prohibits discriminatory practices based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, elderliness, familial status, source of funds, sexual orientation, gender identity, military status, or disability.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: The Virginia Fair Housing Law protects several classes beyond those protected under federal fair housing law. Which of the following is a Virginia-specific protected class not found in the federal Fair Housing Act?
choice_a: Race
choice_b: Religion
choice_c: National origin
choice_d: Source of funds
explanation: Virginia's protected classes include source of funds, sexual orientation, gender identity, military status, and elderliness -- categories the federal Fair Housing Act does not cover.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.1:1, at what age does a person qualify as having reached 'elderliness' for purposes of the Virginia Fair Housing Law's protected classes?
choice_a: 55th birthday
choice_b: 50th birthday
choice_c: 62nd birthday
choice_d: 65th birthday
explanation: 'Elderliness' means an individual who has attained his fifty-fifth birthday.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.1:1, what is required for an animal to qualify as an 'assistance animal'?
choice_a: It must be individually trained and certified
choice_b: It must work, provide assistance, perform tasks, or provide emotional support for a person with a disability -- individual training or certification is not required
choice_c: It must be a dog only
choice_d: It must be registered with the Real Estate Board
explanation: An assistance animal is not required to be individually trained or certified, and species other than dogs can qualify; an assistance animal is not a pet.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2, the 'Mrs. Murphy' -style exemption for a private individual owner selling or renting a single-family house applies only if the owner does not own more than how many single-family houses at one time?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Five
choice_c: Three
choice_d: Ten
explanation: The exemption for a private individual owner applies only if the owner does not own more than three single-family houses at any one time, and other conditions (no use of a real estate licensee, no discriminatory advertising) are met.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(A), does the private-owner single-family-house exemption ever apply to a licensee of the Real Estate Board?
choice_a: Yes, always, if the licensee personally owns the house
choice_b: Yes, but only for broker licensees, not salespersons
choice_c: Yes, but only for licensees who have held their license over 10 years
choice_d: No, this exemption does not apply to or benefit any licensee of the Real Estate Board, regardless of personal or professional capacity
explanation: The private-individual exemption explicitly does not apply to or inure to the benefit of any licensee of the Real Estate Board, whether acting personally or professionally.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(B), the owner-occupied exemption applies to dwellings with living quarters for no more than how many families living independently, if the owner occupies one of the units?
choice_a: Four families
choice_b: Two families
choice_c: Six families
choice_d: Eight families
explanation: This exemption applies to dwellings containing living quarters for no more than four families living independently, where the owner occupies one unit as a residence.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3, is the use of words or symbols associated with a particular religion, national origin, sex, or race in a housing advertisement generally treated as evidence of an illegal preference?
choice_a: No, this is never evidence of a violation
choice_b: Yes, it is prima facie evidence of an illegal preference, not overcome by a general disclaimer -- though a bare reference to a place of worship alone is not
choice_c: Only if the advertisement is in a printed newspaper
choice_d: Only if a formal complaint is filed within 10 days
explanation: Such words/symbols are prima facie evidence of an illegal preference that a general disclaimer cannot overcome, but mere reference to a place of worship (church, synagogue, temple, mosque) alone is not prima facie evidence.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3(B), what must a housing provider do, at the disabled person's expense, regarding reasonable modifications to existing premises?
choice_a: Refuse all modification requests to preserve property value
choice_b: Pay for all modifications out of pocket
choice_c: Permit reasonable modifications necessary for full enjoyment of the premises, though a landlord may condition permission on restoring the interior afterward
choice_d: Modifications are never permitted in rental housing
explanation: Discrimination includes refusing to permit, at the disabled person's expense, reasonable modifications necessary for full enjoyment of the premises; a landlord may reasonably condition permission on restoring the interior later.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3:2, when may a request for a reasonable accommodation be denied?
choice_a: Whenever the housing provider simply prefers not to grant it
choice_b: Reasonable accommodation requests can never be denied
choice_c: Only if the tenant has been late on rent in the past
choice_d: If the person is not disabled, there is no disability-related need, or the accommodation imposes an undue burden or fundamentally alters operations
explanation: A reasonable accommodation request may be denied if the person is not disabled, there's no disability-related need, or the accommodation would impose an undue financial/administrative burden or fundamentally alter operations.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.4, is it unlawful for a lender to require an applicant to financially qualify for a loan?
choice_a: No, it is not unlawful to require an applicant to qualify financially for the loan
choice_b: Yes, this is always considered discriminatory
choice_c: Only for first-time homebuyers
choice_d: Only for loans under $100,000
explanation: It is unlawful to discriminate in residential real estate-related transactions based on protected classes, but it is not unlawful to require an applicant to qualify financially for a loan.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.6, what is the legal status of a restrictive covenant that purports to restrict property occupancy based on race, religion, or another protected class?
choice_a: It is fully enforceable if signed by both parties
choice_b: It is declared void and contrary to the public policy of the Commonwealth
choice_c: It is enforceable only in older deeds recorded before 1970
choice_d: It must be enforced unless a court specifically strikes it
explanation: Restrictive covenants purporting to restrict occupancy or ownership based on protected classes are declared void and contrary to Virginia public policy.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.7, does the familial-status protection apply to qualifying 'housing for older persons'?
choice_a: Yes, equally to all housing
choice_b: It applies only to housing built after 1991
choice_c: No, the familial-status protection does not apply to housing that qualifies as housing for older persons under the statute's criteria
choice_d: It applies only to government-subsidized senior housing
explanation: Familial-status discrimination protections do not apply to qualifying housing for older persons, defined by specific age and occupancy criteria (e.g. at least 80% of units occupied by someone 55+).

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.9, within what time period after an alleged discriminatory housing practice occurred or terminated must a complaint be filed with the Board?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 90 days
choice_c: Two years
choice_d: One year
explanation: A complaint must be filed with the Board in writing within one year after the alleged discriminatory housing practice occurred or terminated.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.10, within how many days after receiving a fair housing complaint must the Board generally complete its investigation?
choice_a: 100 days
choice_b: 60 days
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 180 days
explanation: The Board must commence proceedings within 30 days of receiving a complaint and complete the investigation within 100 days, unless impracticable, in which case both parties are notified in writing of the reasons.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-260, a licensee found by a court to have violated fair housing laws (with no appeal pending or the time for appeal elapsed) is subject to what?
choice_a: No consequence under Board regulations, since it's a separate legal matter
choice_b: This is listed as a prohibited act under the Board's regulations
choice_c: Only a warning letter with no formal action
choice_d: Automatic reinstatement of a suspended license
explanation: Having been found by a court or administrative body to have violated the Virginia Fair Housing Act or other fair housing laws (with no pending appeal) is listed among the Board's prohibited acts.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-260, if a licensee has a conviction for a disqualifying misdemeanor or felony, how many days does the licensee have to inform the Board in writing?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 15 days
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 60 days
explanation: A licensee must inform the Board in writing within 30 days of a disqualifying conviction described in the prohibited-acts regulation.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-270, acting for more than one client in a transaction governed by the dual/designated agency statutes without first doing what constitutes a conflict of interest?
choice_a: Nothing further is required as long as the licensee discloses verbally
choice_b: Notifying the Real Estate Board within 24 hours
choice_c: Paying a disclosure fee
choice_d: Obtaining the written consent of all clients
explanation: Acting for more than one client in a transaction governed by the dual/designated agency statutes without first obtaining written consent of all clients constitutes a conflict of interest.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-280, may a real estate salesperson accept compensation for licensed real estate activity from someone other than their own principal or supervising broker?
choice_a: Only with the prior written consent of the licensee's principal broker
choice_b: Yes, freely, with no restriction
choice_c: Only if the amount is under $500
choice_d: This is always permitted for broker-level licensees only
explanation: A salesperson or associate broker may not accept compensation for licensed real estate activity from anyone other than their own principal/supervising broker without that broker's prior written consent.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-280(A)(5), what kind of listing or lease arrangement is specifically flagged as improper financial dealing?
choice_a: A flat-fee listing arrangement
choice_b: A 'net' listing that lets the licensee sell or lease at any price above a stated net amount and keep the excess
choice_c: A percentage-based commission structure
choice_d: An exclusive-right-to-sell listing
explanation: A 'net' listing/lease providing a set return to the seller/lessor while leaving the licensee free to keep any excess above that price is flagged as improper financial dealing.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-300, using 'bait and switch' advertising -- advertising property with no intent to actually sell or rent at the advertised price -- is what kind of prohibited act?
choice_a: A conflict of interest
choice_b: Improper delivery of instruments
choice_c: Misrepresentation or omission
choice_d: Not a violation if the property is eventually sold to someone
explanation: 'Bait and switch' tactics -- advertising with no intent to sell/rent at the advertised terms, absent proper disclaimers -- constitute misrepresentation or omission.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-300(6), during a dual representation, may a licensee disclose confidential information about one client to the other client represented in that same dual representation?
choice_a: Yes, freely, since both are technically the licensee's clients
choice_b: Only with the supervising broker's verbal approval
choice_c: Only financial information may be shared, not personal information
choice_d: No, unless otherwise provided by law, this is prohibited as misrepresentation or omission
explanation: Disclosing confidential information from one client to the other client in the same dual representation is prohibited (as misrepresentation/omission) unless otherwise provided by law.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-310, at the completion of a real estate transaction, what must a licensee generally deliver to the seller and buyer, unless a settlement agent already discloses it?
choice_a: A complete and accurate statement of receipts and disbursements of moneys received by the licensee, signed and certified by the principal/supervising broker
choice_b: A copy of the licensee's own professional resume
choice_c: A copy of the licensee's continuing education transcript
choice_d: Nothing further is required after closing
explanation: The licensee must deliver a signed and certified statement of receipts and disbursements at closing, unless the disbursement is already disclosed on a settlement statement prepared by a different settlement agent.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-310(3), if a client demands the return of a document or instrument the licensee possesses, what is the licensee required to do?
choice_a: Retain it indefinitely regardless of the request
choice_b: Surrender it to the rightful owner upon demand, absent just cause to refuse
choice_c: Charge a retrieval fee before returning it
choice_d: Only return it after the transaction fully closes
explanation: A licensee must surrender any document or instrument possessed to the rightful owner upon demand, unless there is just cause to refuse or fail to do so.
